## Structure and components

- [statement] The readme-ai generator emits a fixed skeleton: header with badges and logo, project introduction, features table, project structure, project index, getting started (install, usage, tests), community and contributing, license; it offers emoji theme packs prefixed to section titles. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23) — https://github.com/eli64s/readme-ai · keywords: README and changelog boilerplate tells · also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Signs_of_AI_writing

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Detection tools for AI text score poorly in independent testing (all under 80% accuracy, five over 70%), so a formatting tell in a README is grounds to review, not proof of AI authorship. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/pdf/2306.15666 · keywords: README and changelog boilerplate tells · also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Signs_of_AI_writing

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Wikipedia's AI-writing guide lists emoji used as formatting, Markdown syntax, excess boldface, vertical lists with inline headers, and skipped or heading-only-heading structures as signs of AI text, and says they are signs of a possible problem, not the problem itself. (high confidence) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Signs_of_AI_writing · keywords: README and changelog boilerplate tells · also: https://github.com/conorbronsdon/avoid-ai-writing
- [statement] LLM changelog generation can produce entries that are fluent, correctly formatted and false, such as inferring an extra change that never shipped or inventing a value like a cache TTL; the recommended control is human review of the draft. (low confidence) — https://dev.to/nazar-boyko/ai-agents-for-release-notes-and-changelog-automation-kia · keywords: README and changelog boilerplate tells
- [statement] The avoid-ai-writing skill (74 pattern categories, deterministic detector, CI and pre-commit integration) treats generic conclusions, chatbot artifacts and formatting inconsistencies as tells that can be linted in docs. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23) — https://github.com/conorbronsdon/avoid-ai-writing · keywords: README and changelog boilerplate tells
